newsitem.title: USA: American Biogenetic gets FDA clearance.
newsitem.headline: American Biogenetic gets FDA clearance.

text.p: American Biogenetic Sciences Inc said Tuesday that it filed a 510(k) pre-market notification with the Food and Drug Administration for clearance to market its patented Functional Intact Fibrinogen (FiF) test for the quantitative determination of fibrinogen in human plasma.

Elevated fibrinogen levels are recognized as a risk factor for coronary heart disease. Fibrinogen is the protein component that forms fibrin, which builds blood clots that can lead to myocardial infarction (heart attack). Thus, ABS' FiF assay, which is specific and reproducible, is an excellent candidate for cardiovascular risk assessment and population screening.

Recent research reports suggest that fibrinogen is an independent risk factor of cardiovascular disease. It has been reported that an individual with normal cholesterol but elevated fibrinogen levels may be at risk for myocardial infarction, stroke or other thrombotic (blood clots) disorders. It is believed that routine measurement of fibrinogen will become commonplace in diagnostic medicine.
For patient risk management, this test could be performed each time a cholesterol test is performed. There are about 350 million cholesterol tests performed annually worldwide.

The FiF assay is the second test in ABS' product pipeline. ABS' first commercial diagnostic test TpP (thrombus precursor protein) is an in vitro diagnostic test for the risk assessment of blood clot formation (thrombosis) that has been cleared for marketing by the FDA. The test measures soluble fibrin polymers (the precursor to a bloodclot), which have been shown to be elevated in patients at risk of thrombosis.

Elevated soluble fibrin polymer levels have been identified with various clinical conditions, including myocardial infarction, deep vein thrombosis, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and in patients undergoing surgical procedures who are experiencing thrombotic complications.
ABS has marketing-and-sales agreements in place for its TpP test with three companies: Abbott Laboratories, F. Hoffmann La Roche Ltd Ltd, and Gull Laboratories.
